property_summary: For any caller and any provided _unlockTime, after calling Put with some msg.value the contract's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is always at least the block.timestamp (i.e., cannot be set to a past time); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it below block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any Put call with an arbitrary _unlockTime and msg.value>0, the reference contract always sets Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it never sets an unlock in the past), whereas the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it < block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any Put call with msg.value >= 0, the reference contract always sets Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put returns (it clamps to now if _unlockTime is earlier), whereas the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

After any Put call with any _unlockTime and positive msg.value, the reference contract ensures Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps future/past to now), whereas the mutant directly assigns _unlockTime and can leave unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any Put call with msg.value > 0, the reference contract ensures Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never set to a value less than the previous stored unlockTime for that caller (Put clamps unlockTime to at least block.timestamp, so repeated Put cannot reduce the stored unlockTime), while the mutant that directly assigns _unlockTime can lower an account's unlockTime for some fuzzed inputs, violating this monotonicity.

For any caller and any value sent, after calling Put(unlockTime) the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by exactly the sent msg.value (so c.Acc(addr).balance >= previous balance and equals previous+msg.value); the mutant that omits adding msg.value breaks this (balance does not increase for some inputs).

For any caller and any sent value >= MinSum, after calling Put(unlockTime) the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by at least MinSum (i.e., is >= MinSum), but the mutant that omits adding msg.value can leave balance < MinSum for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value, after calling Put(unlockTime) the contract's recorded Acc[caller].unlockTime is set to at least block.timestamp and the contract's recorded Acc[caller].balance increases by msg.value when the caller previously had a nonzero balance OR when msg.value>0 and previous balance==0 the resulting balance equals msg.value; the mutant that omits adding msg.value can leave balance unchanged for some fuzzed (caller, msg.value) and thus violates that balance increased by msg.value.

For every caller and every sent ETH amount, after calling Put(...) the contract's recorded Acc[caller].balance increases by at least the sent msg.value (i.e., new balance >= old balance + msg.value); the mutant that omits adding msg.value can leave the recorded balance unchanged for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any sent value, calling Put(unlockTime) preserves the invariant that the contract's public Acc[caller].balance is at least as large as it was before plus the sent msg.value; the mutant that omits adding msg.value can leave Acc[caller].balance unchanged for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any msg.value and _unlockTime, Put always increases the caller's stored balance by msg.value and sets unlockTime to at least block.timestamp (i.e., acc.balance_new == acc.balance_old + msg.value and acc.unlockTime_new >= block.timestamp); the mutant that sets unlockTime before updating balance can allow an observable state where balance update is not reflected as expected (due to interactions with reentrancy protections and ordering), causing the invariant to fail for some inputs.

After any Put(...) call by a caller, the caller's recorded balance in Acc[msg.sender] increases by exactly msg.value (i.e., newBalance == oldBalance + msg.value); the mutant that sets unlockTime before updating balance can be reentered during LogFile.AddMessage() (which calls external code in Log) and cause the balance increase to be observable as not applied for some inputs.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) with msg.value, the contract's stored balance Acc[caller].balance increases by msg.value (newBalance == oldBalance + msg.value); the mutant that sets unlockTime before updating balance can be re-entered through LogFile.AddMessage (external call) and break this invariant for some inputs.

After any successful Put(...) call by any caller with any msg.value, the caller's recorded unlockTime is at least the block timestamp at the end of the call (i.e., Acc[msg].unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant that swaps setting unlockTime before increasing balance can be reentered through LogFile.AddMessage and leave unlockTime observable below block.timestamp for some inputs, breaking this rule.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value and any _unlockTime, after a successful Put call the caller's stored balance equals the sum of its previous stored balance plus msg.value even if the callee invoked by LogFile.AddMessage re-enters; the mutant can be re-entered during AddMessage to observe a state where the balance was not yet increased, violating newBalance == oldBalance + msg.value.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinSum the reference contract always allows a subsequent Put call (nonReentrant unlocks), so two sequential Put calls from the same address both succeed (no permanent lock), whereas the buggy mutant that omits unlocking makes the second Put revert/fail for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after a successful Put call the contract remains unlocked allowing a second Put from the same caller to succeed; the mutant that omits resetting locked_ breaks this by permanently locking the contract so a subsequent Put from the same caller fails for some inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount >= 0, calling Put twice in sequence from the same externally-owned-account succeeds on the correct contract (nonReentrant_ resets locked_), while the mutant that omits resetting locked_ will make the second Put call fail for some inputs (the contract becomes permanently locked).

After a successful Put call by any externally owned account, the contract remains callable again (Put does not permanently lock the contract); the mutant that omits unlocking the nonReentrant_ modifier makes a subsequent Put call from the same caller fail for some inputs.

For any caller address A and any nonzero payable amount, after A successfully calls Put once the contract remains unlocked so A can successfully call Put a second time; the mutant that omits resetting locked_ makes the second Put call fail (contract stays locked) for some inputs.
After one successful Put by this test contract, a subsequent Put from this contract must not revert (i.e., reentrancy guard resets so second Put succeeds).

A single successful call to Collect by this caller never leaves the contract in a permanently-locked state that causes a subsequent Collect call (with same args) to revert due to the reentrancy guard.

A single external call to Collect(...) from this test account never leaves the contract in a state where a subsequent immediate Collect(...) call from the same account reverts (i.e., if the first Collect does not revert, the second Collect with same args also does not revert).
If a single call to Collect(...) from this caller succeeds (does not revert), then a subsequent immediate call to Collect(...) with the same amount from the same caller must also succeed.

If calling Collect(...) reverts for a caller with insufficient balance or not-yet-unlocked funds, then it must revert again for the same arguments (reentrancy guard should not cause additional unexpected success), and conversely if it succeeds it must not leave the contract permanently locked so that a subsequent immediate Collect with the same args from the same caller does not revert.

After any successful call to Collect by an account that had sufficient balance, the reference contract always allows a subsequent call (the reentrancy lock is cleared), whereas the mutant leaves the contract permanently locked preventing further Collect calls from the same account (or any account) — the test checks that two successive Collect calls both succeed on the reference but the mutant will make the second fail for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller, after a successful Collect that withdraws an amount ≤ their balance and when unlockTime passed, the reference contract allows a subsequent Collect of the same caller (i.e. the second Collect call does not permanently revert due to reentrancy lock), whereas the mutant that never resets the reentrancy lock can make the second Collect call revert; the test fuzzes caller and amount and checks that two sequential Collect calls both succeed on the reference.

For any caller and amount where Put then Collect succeeds once (balance≥MinSum, balance≥amount, unlockTime passed), the reference contract allows a subsequent Collect call to succeed (reentrancy lock is cleared), whereas the mutant that never clears the lock will make that second Collect revert — so: after a successful Collect, a second Collect with same conditions still succeeds on the reference but can fail on the mutant.

For any caller and amounts where Put then Collect succeeds once (satisfying MinSum, balance≥amount, and unlockTime passed), the reference contract does NOT remain locked and therefore subsequent calls to Put (which uses nonReentrant_) still succeed; the mutant that never resets the lock will make a subsequent Put (or any call using nonReentrant_) revert for some inputs.

After any successful Collect call by an address that withdraws funds, the reference contract clears the nonReentrant_ lock so that a subsequent external call to Put (which uses the same nonReentrant_ modifier) by any address can still succeed (does not revert); the mutant that never resets the lock can leave the contract permanently locked causing such a subsequent Put to revert for some inputs.
After a successful Collect call the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance decreases by the collected amount and the contract's ETH balance decreases by the same amount.
If the caller's Acc[msg.sender].balance is at least MinSum and at least the requested amount and unlocked, then Collect never reverts (i.e., completes) for all such inputs.

If the caller requests to Collect an amount _am that is no more than the contract's current ETH balance, then Collect should not revert (i.e., should complete) on the original — the mutant that uses transfer can revert when the contract lacks the 2300 gas stipend or when sending from a contract with limited gas, so require that address(c).balance >= _am ensures original succeeds but mutant may revert.

When caller's Acc[msg.sender].balance >= MinSum, >= _am, unlocked, and the caller is an EOA (not a contract), Collect should not revert on the original but may revert for the mutant that uses transfer to send to a contract — so require the caller is a contract by making this test contract call Collect, and assert that Collect does not revert (reverted == false).

When caller (this test contract) has sufficient recorded balance, requests <= that balance, and unlock time passed, Collect on the original never reverts when the recipient is a contract that can accept a transfer paying gas, but may revert for the mutant which uses transfer; so for inputs where this test contract's fallback consumes more than 2300 gas, original completes but mutant reverts.
